items.reasoning: No engineer was booked. A4 only asks HeatRight for availability and a price, and the answer says 'No contractor assigned and no visit booked'. No 24-hour written notice was given; it is only promised. The new tenant contacts used email and SMS again, which had already been tried. The phone call and letter were only scheduled as a follow-up for 12 Oct, on a tight deadline.
items.evidence: "No contractor assigned and no visit booked"; A4 asks for availability only

items.reasoning: A5 is a verified email to Ben. It covers the 16 Oct deadline, Luca's lack of reply since 25 Sep, the steps taken (job opened, tenant re-contacted, HeatRight asked) and the lawful access approach.

items.reasoning: The ticket JOB-101 description records the earlier attempts (email 25/9, email and SMS 2/10). The new email and SMS are logged against the ticket (MSG-102, MSG-103). The follow-up also mentions escalating with documented attempts.

items.reasoning: A6 schedules a follow-up for 12 Oct to phone Luca and send an access-notice letter, and to escalate to compliance (a human) if there is still no access by 13 Oct. That is a dated conditional escalation with a letter step, though hand delivery is not stated explicitly.

The remaining-work list includes giving the tenant a copy of the new CP12 within 28 days.

items.reasoning: Compliance is based on the formal record, not the legacy note.
The agent says explicitly that there will be no entry without notice. It did not force entry or plan to.

items.reasoning: The agent says the certificate lapses after 16 Oct and that being compliant today does not guarantee compliance afterwards.
items.evidence: "Compliance today does not guarantee compliance after 16 Oct."

grades.overall_note: The agent read compliance status correctly, kept access lawful and kept the landlord informed. It fell short on urgency: six days before expiry it only asked HeatRight for availability rather than booking a slot, and it gave no written notice. It also never mentioned the two-month anniversary rule.
